Chinese Stock Markets Can't Quite Shake Off Bearish Sentiment
sum: Chinese stock markets remained on edge this week, with investor sentiment tilting bearish and tech shares remaining under pressure as the shock from the resignation of high-profile Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang reverberated through global markets.

The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index fell 0.6 percent on Friday and 0.4 percent for the week. Its Nasdaq-style STAR Market 50 index tumbled 2.3 percent on Friday but managed a 1.8 percent gain for the week. The Shenzhen Component Index lost 1.9 percent for the week, and the tech-heavy ChiNext board retreated 1.3 percent after tanking 3.3 percent on Friday. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell 1.6 percent on Friday for a weekly loss of 3.5 percent. Its tech index dropped 3 percent.

The sharp decline in tech stocks was, in part, due to Huang's departure from the AI tech giant he co-founded and ran for three decades. He quit after revelations of an extramarital affair. In China's tech realm, Victory Giant Technology and TFC Communications dropped by the daily limit of 10 percent on Friday. Shares in optical transceiver giant Zhongji Innolight tumbled 8.4 percent, Eoptolink lost 8.8 percent, and electronics maker Foxconn retreated 7.5 percent.

"The exit of Jensen Huang from Nvidia is due to have a huge impact, but at the moment, it's unclear how huge," said Dai Qing, an analyst with Changjiang Securities. "Suppliers and customers of Nvidia in China will have to wait for an evaluation, as well as will the rest of the world."

A Morgan Stanley gauge of Chinese mainland investor sentiment from November 5-11 fell 16 percentage points to 15 percent, with trading volumes contracting. The bank said it remains cautious on Chinese stocks, but favors shares traded on the Chinese mainland over those traded in Hong Kong.

Overall, Chinese equities have lost about US$3.5 trillion in value since May. To bolster the market, Beijing has taken steps to facilitate more equity investment by state-backed funds and more company share buybacks. The China Securities Regulatory Commission reiterated at an investor conference in Shanghai on Thursday that "there is long-term certainty in China's development, which lays a solid foundation for investment."

China Stock Market Sees Late-Session Volume Surge in Defensive Buying; Equity ETFs Absorb Nearly CNY 600 Billion Over Two Months
sum: Technology stocks weakened during the November 13 session in mainland China, but trading volume in several broad-based ETFs (exchange-traded funds) suddenly surged in the afternoon, with dense turnover appearing in the closing session — a signal the market interpreted as capital stepping in to absorb selling. Statistics show that from September 28 to November 12, equity ETFs recorded cumulative net inflows of CNY 593.826 billion (approximately $89.0 billion), though flows turned to net outflows over the past three trading days.

On the afternoon of November 13, trading in broad-based ETFs clearly heated up. Tianhong CSI 300 ETF traded CNY 738 million (approximately $110.7 million) for the full day, setting a record since the ETF's listing, with activity concentrated in the closing session. GF CSI 300 ETF traded CNY 336 million (approximately $50.4 million) over the session, of which CNY 279 million (approximately $41.8 million) changed hands in the final 25 minutes — meaning more than 80% of volume was concentrated before the close.

Sector ETFs also saw late-session volume bursts. Huabao Securities ETF traded more than CNY 800 million (approximately $120.0 million) in the final 35 minutes, with full-day turnover of CNY 1.274 billion (approximately $191.0 million); GF Media ETF traded over CNY 300 million (approximately $45.0 million) in the final 20 minutes, with full-day turnover of CNY 891 million (approximately $133.6 million). As for larger flagship products, E Fund ChiNext ETF and ChinaAMC STAR 50 ETF each exceeded CNY 11 billion (approximately $1.6 billion) in single-day turnover, while ChinaAMC STAR Semiconductor ETF also reached CNY 10 billion (approximately $1.5 billion).

Looking at fund flows, this wave of ETF buying has been underway for some time. Since September 28, equity ETFs had recorded net inflows for 26 consecutive trading days before turning to net outflows from November 10 to 12, with net outflows of CNY 25.434 billion (approximately $3.8 billion) on November 12 alone. For the period from September 28 to November 12 combined, net inflows reached CNY 593.826 billion (approximately $89.0 billion).

US stocks rise as CoreWeave eases AI spending fears
sum: NEW YORK: US stocks closed higher on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq each rallying more than 1% as earnings from neocloud firm CoreWeave cooled investor concerns about the durability of the AI trade, while Nvidia stabilized after two straight sessions of sharp declines.
Battered CoreWeave shares surged 24.7%, their biggest daily percentage jump in more than three months, to close at the highest level in two weeks.

The company said it would become profitable in the first half of 2028 on an adjusted basis, seeking to reassure investors that strong demand and customer commitments could support its debt-fueled expansion.
Sentiment improvedacross AI infrastructure stocks, as Nebius Group surged 15.4% and Applied Digital shot up 7.4%.

Nvidia advanced after shedding about US$430 billion of market capitalisation in the previous two sessions as investors worried about CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy.

Equities have been volatile in recent days. Investors have expressed concerns about more regulation in the AI space after sweeping Democratic victories in the US midterm elections last week. That, and worries about Nvidia's leadership, pressured one of the biggest pillars of the current bull market.
Contributing to choppy stock trading, investors have been encouraged by cooling oil prices but concerned by hot inflation data that pushed Treasury yields sharply higher.

Stocks jump as oil tumbles, Nvidia falls amid internal probe
sum: NEW YORK/LONDON: Major stock indexes rallied on Monday as Brent crude oil fell more than 5% after US President Donald Trump said he is unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran, while shares of Nvidia dropped.
The fall in oil prices helped to ease worries about inflation that have weighed on economies across the globe this year.

Trump on Sunday said that he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the war progressed, even though both countries reported that shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures fell $5.75, or 5.85%, to settle at $92.57 a barrel, and prices continued falling after settlement, while US West Texas Intermediate futures dropped $3.98, or 4.38%, to $86.85.
Efforts to end the Iran war have gathered pace following last week's US midterm elections in which Democrats won control of Congress.

Shares of Nvidia, the second-most valuable company in the world, tumbled 4.2% and closed at their lowest level since April 7, with investors questioning CEO Jensen Huang's future at the AI chipmaker after an internal investigation into whether a foreign intelligence effort had targeted him.

However, the three major US stock indexes finished more than 2% higher, with the S&P 500 rebounding from its biggest weekly drop since April 2025. Last week's selloff was tied to the US midterm elections and worries about increased AI and data center regulation.

"We have seen a very steep and exaggerated selloff in the market," said Adam Sarhan, chief executive of 50 Park Investments in New York. "Whenever the market gets that stretched to the downside, history has shown us usually it's a good buying opportunity in the short term."

AI slump revives Asia’s overlooked markets
sum: BEIJING: The unravelling of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade after the US midterm elections is forcing investors to rethink their Asia playbook, reviving demand for out-of-favour Chinese and Indian stocks as well as companies poised to benefit from easing inflation and trade tensions.
Aberdeen Investments favours markets powered by stronger domestic growth, including India and Vietnam, and sees upside in Chinese technology firms.
Hedge fund Lotus Asset Management is long Hong Kong equity futures, while Allianz Global Investors is looking at healthcare and consumer companies.
Asia has been among the hardest hit by the market fallout from the Democrats’ sweep of Congress.

Many of the region’s biggest stocks – from Samsung Electronics Co and SK Hynix Inc to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co – are critical suppliers to the global AI build-out, leaving local markets especially exposed as investors brace for greater scrutiny of the industry and question whether massive spending on computing infrastructure will generate sufficient returns.
“I expect investors to diversify more broadly and reduce their concentration in the AI trade,” said Rajeev De Mello, global macro portfolio manager at Gama Asset Management SA.
“This should be supportive of China and other markets where valuations are less demanding. India could also benefit, although its dependence on imported energy remains a headwind,” he added.

Part of the reason lies in how the rally started. Beijing wanted to depend less on US tech, so state-backed funds poured money into chipmakers, robotics firms and AI labs. Retail investors saw that backing as a signal to buy.

US stock futures dip as investors await midterm election results
sum: SINGAPORE: US stock futures slid and the dollar softened on Wednesday as investors girded for results from US midterm election with the focus on whether Democrats can wrest control of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republicans.
Democrat Jon Ossoff won re-election in Georgia, marking the first significant race call of the night as polls closed in seven states.
Democrats are favoured to capture the House and both parties are locked in an intense state-by-state battle for the Senate, leaving investors and markets on edge.

"For traders, the distinction between a narrow Democratic majority and a commanding victory is critical," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone. "A narrow blue wave may be largely priced in."

In the US Senate, where at least nine races are seen as competitive, Democrats won the first of 35 seats up for grabs on Tuesday, with US Senator Mark Warner winning reelection in Virginia as expected. Democrats need to net four seats to win control of that chamber.
Weston said the greatest market reaction may come not from who wins Congress, but from how decisively they win and how far the result deviates from expectations.
Futures for S&P 500 slid 0.5% while Nasdaq futures fell 0.9%.

items.t: Emerging markets - Asian forex slips ahead of inflation data, Korean stocks buck AI selloff
sum: MANILA (Reuters): Emerging Asian currencies edged lower against the dollar on Monday, while equities were mixed as investors digested the AI rout and awaited a raft of inflation data.

An MSCI gauge of emerging-market currencies slipped 0.2% against a steady dollar as markets looked ahead to US midterm elections that could determine control of Congress and shape spending priorities. The Singapore dollar lost 0.2% and the Taiwan dollar shed 0.6%.

The South Korean won weakened to 1,346.90 per US dollar, its lowest since mid-October. Analysts at MUFG said the won continues to be underpinned by favourable macroeconomic conditions, though persistent foreign selling of equities has diluted support for the currency.
South Korean shares rose 2.2%, with dip-buying in technology stocks helping the market look past the AI-driven selloff on Wall Street on Friday after weak results from Intel and Amazon.
Data showed South Korean exports nearly doubled in October, marking their sharpest increase in more than five decades, as strong global demand for AI investment boosted chip shipments.
Singapore's benchmark stock index slid 1.4%, weighed down by banking stocks ahead of earnings from DBS and OCBC, bringing losses from its early-September record high to nearly 10%.
In Indonesia, stocks fell as much as 1.5% before reversing course to trade up 0.9%, with investors awaiting inflation and third-quarter economic growth data due later this week.

sum: Stocks to buy | Shares to buy | Ganesh Dongre's stock recommendations: The Indian equity benchmarks ended the week on a positive note, with the Nifty gaining nearly 2% to close at 23,053, while the Bank Nifty advanced 0.75% to settle at 54,686. However, the Nifty 50 index witnessed buying interest at lower levels and recovered towards the 23,200 mark, although it continues to face resistance at higher levels. Sectoral performance remained broadly positive, with most major sectors witnessing gains in the range of 2%–7%.

The Pharma sector emerged as the top performer, rallying nearly 7% during the week. However, despite the recovery in domestic equities, Brent crude oil remains elevated, hovering in the $110–$115 per barrel range, keeping inflationary concerns and global uncertainties in focus.

Ganesh Dongre, AVP — Equity Research at Anand Rathi, believes a sustained weekly close of the Nifty 50 index above 23,200–23,400 would improve the near-term technical outlook of the Indian stock market. Ganesh Dongre of Anand Rathi said that both the Nifty 50 and Bank Nifty index remain in a cautious technical phase. The rebound from oversold levels has improved near-term sentiment; however, a sustained recovery will require the Nifty to establish itself above the 23,200–23,400 resistance zone and subsequently reclaim the 24,000–24,200 range. Similarly, the Bank Nifty needs to move decisively above 56,400–56,500 to strengthen its technical outlook.

“Until these crucial resistance levels are convincingly breached, markets are likely to remain volatile, with intermittent recovery attempts, range-bound consolidation and selling pressure at higher levels. Traders should therefore maintain a cautious approach and closely monitor key support and resistance levels, along with Brent crude oil prices and geopolitical developments, for confirmation of the next directional move,” Ganesh Dongre of Anand Rathi said.

Speaking on the Nifty 50 outlook for next week, the Anand Rathi expert said the 50-stock index witnessed a notable rebound from the 22,500–22,200 support zone and recovered towards the 23,200 level by the end of the week.
